\subsection{Integral library and the scaleless rule}
The library (\texttt{P15\_integral\_library.json}) provides $A_0$, $B_0$ and the tensor reduction in $\hat g$. It is
certified exactly in $d$ against Feynman parameters, and numerically at $d=2.6,3.3,3.7$.

The scaleless rule is \emph{stated}, not assumed:
\[
\text{S0:}\quad \int d^dl\,(l^2)^k/(l^2)^\nu := 0, \qquad \omega=4+2k-2\nu .
\]
Its UV/IR reading is as follows. For $\omega=0$ the zero is the cancellation $1/\epsilon_{\rm UV}-1/\epsilon_{\rm IR}$.
For $\omega\neq0$ it discards a pure power divergence, and neither the UV part nor the IR part has a pole at $d=4$.
Applying S0 to an integral that carries a scale is an error, and Missing is never replaced by zero by convention.

\subsection{Batch A: D02, D12, D14a--c}
All five graphs are \emph{vanishing under the declared prescription}: there is no UV pole, the finite part is $0$, and
no p14r counterterm is needed. Every scaleless member is a pure power divergence ($\omega=2,4$), so the zero is
\emph{not} a $1/\epsilon_{\rm UV}-1/\epsilon_{\rm IR}$ cancellation.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{IR-regulator mass} (analysis only). With a mass the poles are proportional to $\kappa^2m^4hh$ and
$\kappa^2m^2p^2hh$, which are order-0/2 contacts excluded by N4, or to $\kappa m^4h$, for which the $\kappa^1$ basis is
empty. All of them vanish as $m\to0$.
\item \textbf{Analytic regulator.} It does not separate the UV from the IR here.
\item \textbf{Cross-check.} Two routes agree: the frozen dred lift with S0, and an independent symmetric tensor
integration.
\item \textbf{D12.} D12 ($\kappa^2\,hh$) is kept separate from the order-$\kappa$ one-point slot (D14a--c).
\texttt{D12\_status} moves from Missing to \emph{vanishing\_under\_declared\_prescription}. This is \emph{derived} under
P's own prescription; XVI-O's value is not imported.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Batch B: D13 ($\kappa^2$ K$'\!\cdot c$)}
Write $G_{(mn)\nu}(p)=V_{\Gamma_1}[K'_{(mn)}(-p),c^\nu(p)]=\kappa^2N_\epsilon\hat G$, with
$\hat G=\sum_iA_i(d)\,T_i\,B_0$, $B_0=1/\epsilon+2-L$ and $L=\log(-p^2/\mu^2-i0)$. The structures are
\[
T_1=\eta_{mn}p_\nu p^2,\quad T_2=(\eta_{m\nu}p_n+\eta_{n\nu}p_m)p^2,\quad T_3=p_mp_np_\nu,
\]
together with the evanescent $E_1=\tilde G_{mn}p_\nu p^2$ and $E_2=(\tilde G_{m\nu}p_n+\tilde G_{n\nu}p_m)p^2$. The
coefficients are
\[
A_{T_2}=\frac{4d-7}{16(d-1)},\qquad A_{T_3}=\frac{3(2-d)}{8(d-1)},\qquad A_{E_2}=\frac{3}{16(d-1)},\qquad
A_{T_1}=A_{E_1}=0 .
\]
This gives:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{UV poles:} $T_2$: $3/16$, $T_3$: $-1/4$, $E_2$: $1/16$.
\item \textbf{MS-bar finite parts:} $T_2$: $1/3-\tfrac{3}{16}L$, $T_3$: $-5/12+\tfrac14L$, $E_2$: $1/6-\tfrac1{16}L$.
The nonlocal part is $-(\text{pole})\cdot L$, and the local part is a cubic polynomial.
\item \textbf{Counterterm map.} The 4D pole lies in the span of the three p14r $c\cdot K'$ directions, with coordinates
$(0,3/8,-1/4)$. The local ambiguity is a finite renormalization along the same directions.
\item \textbf{$d$-dependence.} The $(d-4)\times$pole terms shift the local part ($T_2$: $-1/24$, $T_3$: $+1/12$).
Setting $d=4$ first gives a different MS-bar finite part.
\item \textbf{Evanescent pole and status.} The evanescent pole ($E_2$) is nonzero, and the p14r contract declares no
evanescent counterterm. D13's status is therefore \emph{regulated}. Its 4D sector is \emph{renormalized}; the
evanescent pole is recorded but not absorbed, and stays an open contract item.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Controls.}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Two routes, exact in $d$.} Route 1 is the sha-pinned export through the dred Pipeline. Route 2 is the
integrand regenerated from the rule tables and evaluated by Feynman parameters with $d$ symbolic. They agree exactly.
\item \textbf{Exact covariant fit.}
\item \textbf{BRST sanity (ghost equation).} $2i\,D^\rho[G]$ equals the evaluated one-loop ghost self-energy. The
ghost self-energy's 4D pole lies in the p14r $c\cdot\bar c$ span, at $(-3/8,1/4)$; its evanescent pole is $-1/8$.
\item \textbf{Structural R5 safeguard.} It is active.
\end{itemize}
\paragraph{Mutations.} Each mutation changes the result and is rejected: wrong ghost-loop sign, premature $d=4$ (refused
at the substitution), dropped evanescent part, wrong symmetry factor, and wrong K$'$/$c$ ordering.

\subsection{Disclosed p14r contract revision}
Finding F1 of the p14r independent rebuild concerns the p14r \texttt{PrematureD4Substitution} guard in
\texttt{dred.py}, which was a heuristic.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{What went wrong.} It gave a false positive on
$\eta^{rs}\!\int l_rl_s/(l^2-m^2)=J$, a correct $d$-free result. It gave a false negative under the premature-$d=4$
mutation on the same integral: the result was $dJ/4$, a finite error of $-m^4/2$.
\item \textbf{What p15 does.} p15 replaces the guard by a structural, provenance-based safeguard. $d$ is opaque and can
be substituted only through \texttt{dred.substitute\_d}, which records each use. Numeric traces of $\hat g/\tilde g$ are
refused. The R5 docstring is corrected, and the reviewer's toys are regression tests.
\item \textbf{What does not change.} R1--R6 are unchanged, and every other contract file is byte-identical (checked
against pinned sha256). Released p14r values are unaffected, since p14r applied the Laurent step only to toys.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Reproducibility}
The independent rebuild of p14r \emph{passed}: 143/143 values equal and 60 tests. It is bound to the p14r tree
\texttt{a64c0ae3\ldots} and zip \texttt{19e8bf59\ldots}. It ran on the same box, in a fresh directory and venv, and was
not run on a second machine. It is not inherited by p15, whose own independent flag is pending.
